findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive boolean flag that allows the invalid state {is_validated=false, is_sent=true} -- a packet cannot be sent before it is validated.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can mark a packet as sent while is_validated is false, violating the domain invariant that only validated packets may be sent. The compiler cannot enforce ordering or mutual exclusion between these two booleans.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single typestate enum such as enum PacketLifecycle { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } } and make the PacketWorkflow struct carry this enum instead of two independent booleans.

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary string values (e.g. "sent", "deleted", "foobar") that do not correspond to any valid lifecycle step. The mark_sent function only sets status to "sent" but never validates that the previous status was a valid predecessor.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct PacketWorkflow with status="foobar" and bypass all domain state transitions. The type system cannot distinguish valid from invalid status strings, making illegal states representable at runtime.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed enum PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }. Use a fallible constructor or enum variants that encode the transition logic so invalid strings are unrepresentable.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is independent of the boolean is_sent. The invalid state {is_sent=false, sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(123)} is constructible, as is {is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=None}.
findings.failure_mode: The Option field allows a sent timestamp to exist without the packet being in a sent state, or vice versa. Any code reading sent_at_epoch_ms must defensively check is_sent first, creating a fragile implicit contract.
findings.fix: Tie sent_at_epoch_ms inside the Sent variant of the PacketLifecycle typestate enum so a timestamp can only exist when the packet is in the Sent state. Remove is_sent and sent_at_epoch_ms as separate fields.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs a state transition without any validation of preconditions. It unconditionally sets status to "sent" and is_sent to true regardless of whether is_validated is true.
findings.failure_mode: The function has no way to reject invalid transitions. It silently corrupts the domain invariant by allowing a non-validated packet to enter the sent state. This should return a Result or use an enum-based typestate where the transition is only possible from Validated.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept a PacketLifecycle::Validated and return PacketLifecycle::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms }. The compiler will reject all invalid transitions at compile time, and the function signature itself documents the precondition.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for the PacketWorkflow struct or mark_sent function. Performance claims (even trivial ones) require measured evidence per Holzman discipline.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmarks, there is no evidence that the data shape or transition logic performs acceptably under real workload pressure. Future refactors could introduce regressions undetected.
findings.fix: Add a micro-benchmark (e.g., criterion or a simple timed loop) measuring PacketWorkflow construction and mark_sent execution.

findings.problem: No test module exists to verify the PacketWorkflow lifecycle invariants. There is no proof that valid transitions are accepted and invalid ones are rejected.
findings.failure_mode: Without behavior tests, regressions to the typestate transitions go undetected. The absence of tests also means there is no executable contract for future reviewers.
findings.fix: Add a tests/ module with tests covering: valid transition Pending->Validated->Sent, and compile-time or runtime rejection of invalid transitions like Pending->Sent.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for PacketWorkflow construction and mark_sent execution
no allocation profiling evidence for PacketWorkflow heap usage (3 String fields + Option)
no behavior tests verifying lifecycle transition invariants
no second-ring review (proof-plan or black-hat) evidence
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has zero production unsafe/unwrap/expect violations, but the fundamental type discipline problem (boolean flags and String status allowing illegal states) is a BLOCKER that must be resolved before delivery. The struct is trivially small so performance risk is low, but unmeasured.
